compiled_state.title: As a maintainer, every LiteLLM completion call has provider-chain and tier-upgrade fallbacks configured with a fallback_exhausted signal in a documented schema
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Wire LiteLLM `fallbacks=[...]` (cross-provider) and `context_window_fallbacks=[...]` (same-provider tier upgrade) into every `litellm.completion(...)` call in `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` with `streaming=False` mandated, plus a structured `fallback_exhausted` JSON entry on full-chain failure conformant to `docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`.

**Why**: Today CI review aborts on a single transient `RateLimitError` from the primary provider. With this in place, a 429 on Anthropic transparently routes to OpenAI via LiteLLM's reliability primitives; a context-window overflow on a tier-N model upgrades to tier-N+1 on the same provider. When both fallback lists are exhausted, the dispatcher writes a structured `fallback_exhausted` entry consumed by a future Copilot-reviewer-terminal-gate epic. Establishes the substrate signal that Flow B's merge gate depends on.

**Scope**:
- IN: `fallbacks` and `context_window_fallbacks` parameter rendering from `dso-config.conf` key `ci_review.provider_chain` × agent `model:` field; `streaming=False` enforced everywhere; terminal exception caught at `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError` base; `fallback_exhausted` entry with all 6 documented fields; atomic write (temp + rename); per-agent file ownership documented; PR review summary hop rendering in stable format `[fallback: <agent> <primary_model> -> <fallback_model> (<exception_class>)]`; startup precondition rejecting missing provider credentials with a clear error; strict provider-name parsing (lowercase canonical only; whitespace trimmed; unknown providers reject at config-load time); contract documented at `docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`.
- OUT: Cross-provider fallback for `ContextWindowExceededError` (kept routed to same-provider ladder; opus-tier terminal case documented); the downstream Copilot-reviewer-gate workflow itself (separate epic); cache-cliff mitigation when fallback fires mid-multi-turn-run (deferred to integration with 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, every `litellm.completion(...)` call in `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` is constructed with `streaming=False`, `fallbacks=[...]` rendered from `ci_review.provider_chain`, and `context_window_fallbacks=[...]` rendered from the agent's `model:` upgraded through `[haiku, sonnet, opus]` on the agent's primary provider
  ← Satisfies: "Provider chain + tier-upgrade fallback via LiteLLM, with `fallback_exhausted` signal..."
- When this story is complete, a 429 on the primary provider transparently completes the review on the alternate provider, with a `[fallback: <agent> <primary> -> <fallback> (<exception_class>)]` line rendered in the PR review summary
  ← Satisfies: "successful fallback hops as one-line notes in the PR review summary in stable format"
- When this story is complete, full chain exhaustion produces a `fallback_exhausted` JSON entry conformant to `docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md` with fields `agent_id`, `primary_model`, `attempted_cross_provider[]`, `attempted_context_models[]`, `final_exception_class`, `final_exception_message`; the entry is written atomically (temp + rename) and surviving agents' partial findings are preserved per c6de SC4
  ← Satisfies: "writes a `fallback_exhausted` entry into `reviewer-findings.json` ... conforming to a documented schema"
- When this story is complete, dispatcher startup refuses to run with a clear error when any provider in `ci_review.provider_chain` lacks credentials in the runtime environment, and `provider_chain` parsing rejects unknown / non-canonical / case-incorrect provider names at config-load time
  ← Satisfies: "Startup precondition: dispatcher refuses to run with a clear error when any provider in `ci_review.provider_chain` lacks credentials"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic cover: `RateLimitError` -> alternate provider answers; `ContextWindowExceededError` -> next tier-model on same provider; full-chain failure -> `fallback_exhausted` JSON entry; contract-conformance test loading the schema; `streaming=False` preservation across hops; startup-time rejection on missing provider credentials
  ← Satisfies: "Verified by: (a) unit test injecting RateLimitError... (b) ContextWindowExceededError... (c) full-chain failure... (d) contract conformance test... (e) streaming=False preservation... (f) startup-time rejection"

## Considerations

- [Reliability] LiteLLM SDK-level `fallbacks` / `context_window_fallbacks` is the documented happy path but has zero popular OSS adoption (LiteLLM Router is more battle-tested); plain-text completion path verified working but watch for edge cases.
- [Reliability] LiteLLM streaming-mode fallback has confirmed open bugs (#22296, #6532) — `streaming=False` mandate is non-negotiable; tests must assert `streaming` parameter is False at every hop including fallback entries.
- [Security] `provider_chain` parsing must reject unknown / case-variant provider names at config-load time, not silently produce empty fallback list (which would defeat fallback without operator-visible error).
- [Reliability] `fallback_exhausted` partial-write corruption is real when deep tier dispatches 3 specialists + arch synthesis writing to the same `reviewer-findings.json` — atomic write (temp + rename) plus documented per-agent file ownership in the contract is required.
- [Maintainability] Cross-provider switch wastes Anthropic prompt cache built up earlier in a multi-turn run (interaction with 2fa0 SC3); mitigation deferred to integration time once both epics are merged. Document the cost-cliff possibility in the schema's notes section.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
